home.about.title: About
home.about.intro: fancy-ui-react is the React 18 and 19 counterpart of
home.about.sibling-tail: : 144 components exported from the package root, the sound family beside them, and the cameleon skin engine on the
home.about.paragraph-2: Styled with Tailwind CSS v4. Two imports are the whole setup, the semantic colour tokens ship with defaults you can override, and dark mode follows the operating system until you put a class on the root element.
home.about.paragraph-3: ESM only, four entry points and one module per source file, so the components you do not import tree-shake away. Every component module carries the client directive, so it drops straight into a Server Component tree.

home.projects.intro: Three families from the catalogue, each rendered live on this page by the package itself.
home.projects.motion.title: Motion & cursors
home.projects.motion.description: FluidCursor paints the hero on WebGPU with a WebGL fallback, InteractiveGridPattern lights the squares under your pointer, BlurReveal staggers the copy in, and ImageTrailCursor waits at the bottom of the page.
home.projects.motion.caption: LIVE · HOVER THE FRAME
home.projects.overlays.title: Overlays & forms
home.projects.overlays.description: Dialog, AlertDialog, Sheet, Drawer, Popover and the menus share one portal, focus trap, scroll lock and dismiss layer. Form controls follow the React split: uncontrolled by default, controlled once you pass a value.
home.projects.overlays.caption: PORTAL · FOCUS TRAP · SCROLL LOCK
home.projects.overlays.dialog.title: Dialog
home.projects.overlays.dialog.descriptio: Rendered by fancy-ui-react from a Server Component. Escape, the close button and a click outside all dismiss it.
home.projects.overlays.dialog.body: Focus is trapped while it is open and returns to the trigger when it closes. The page behind it stops scrolling until then.
home.projects.skins.title: Cameleon skins
home.projects.skins.description: FancyProvider wraps a subtree in a skin — default, aurora, brutal, glass, terminal or retro-os — and the primitives repaint through its tokens. Two of them are running further down this page.
home.projects.footnote: Every component on this page is imported from the published entry points. Only the page layout around them is local.
home.testimonials.title: From the docs
home.testimonials.subtitle: Hover a file to see where each line comes from; click a card to read it in context
testimonials.1.excerpt: Components and hooks are client modules. Import them from a Server Component file and they cross the boundary as client references, which is exactly what you want: no "use client" wrapper of your own, and no useState running on the server.
testimonials.1.body.1: Components and hooks are client modules. Import them from a Server Component file and they cross the boundary as client references, which is exactly what you want: no "use client" wrapper of your own, and no useState running on the server. The examples/next-app App Router example in this repo is a Server Component that imports the whole barrel, and it is part of CI.
testimonials.2.excerpt: Out of the box the package follows the operating-system preference: dark: utilities and the components' light-dark() colours both switch with prefers-color-scheme, so an app that never touches dark mode already looks right on a dark desktop.
testimonials.2.body.1: Out of the box the package follows the operating-system preference: dark: utilities and the components' light-dark() colours both switch with prefers-color-scheme, so an app that never touches dark mode already looks right on a dark desktop. To control it yourself, put dark or light on <html> (or on any ancestor of the subtree you want to force) and both halves follow the class instead: <html class="dark">
testimonials.2.body.2: tailwind.css is what makes that work, in three parts: it declares the .dark token block, it declares a dark variant that matches a .dark ancestor OR the media query (unless a .light ancestor opts out), and it sets color-scheme: light dark on :root with .dark / .light overrides so the components' light-dark() colours — and the browser's own form controls, scrollbars and caret — resolve the same way. An app that declares its own @custom-variant dark after the import keeps its own definition.
testimonials.3.excerpt: Nothing may differ between a server render and its hydration. No Math.random(), Date.now() or window read in a render path or a lazy useState initializer.
testimonials.3.body.1: Nothing may differ between a server render and its hydration. No Math.random(), Date.now() or window read in a render path or a lazy useState initializer. Where the Svelte source randomises, take a seed prop and use a deterministic PRNG, and record it as a divergence in the README.
testimonials.4.excerpt: The sound prop must work with zero setup. It is an ordinary boolean prop on button, checkbox, copy-button, dropdown-menu, radio-group, select and switch.
testimonials.4.body.1: The sound prop must work with zero setup. It is an ordinary boolean prop on button, checkbox, copy-button, dropdown-menu, radio-group, select and switch. A provider would make <Button sound /> silently do nothing in an unwrapped tree — a real API break against the Svelte package, landing as a support burden on seven components' users. The source's own stated reason for the singleton is that sound.play() must be callable from anywhere, including code that is not inside a React tree.
testimonials.4.body.2: The state is genuinely global — one localStorage key, one cross-tab storage listener, one AudioContext. Two providers would be two truths for one key.
home.passions.title: Beyond components
home.passions.subtitle: Two things the package ships that are not a component: an interface sound layer and a skin engine
home.passions.sound.title: Sound design
home.passions.sound.description: Every interactive component takes an opt-in sound prop. It stays silent until the person using the page enables sound, then plays a short synthesised cue from one shared Web Audio engine: no audio files, no provider.
home.passions.sound.hint: Enable sound, then press the button.
home.passions.cameleon.title: Cameleon skins
home.passions.cameleon.description: One provider, six skins. Each skin is a token recipe the primitives read at render time, so the same tree can look brutalist, glassy or like a retro desktop without a rebuild.
